passages.text: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
passages.note: when silence is wiser than advice

passages.text: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble. He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
passages.note: the brevity and trouble of human life

passages.text: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease. Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground, yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.

“I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters! Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer? I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you, but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you. “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
passages.note: unhelpful comfort; grief that talking doesn't ease

passages.text: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.
My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
